strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck in multimodal models. Reducing 576 visual tokens to approximately 40 through class-attention selection and key-based merging is a simple, potentially useful approach that also supports training-free application.
Evaluation covers six benchmarks and both 7B and 13B LLaVA-1.5 models. Despite substantial compression, fine-tuned models preserve or improve POPE performance and retain strong ScienceQA results.

The ablations provide useful supporting evidence: training-free PruMerge improves TextVQA over spatial sampling (54.00 versus at most 47.96 in Table 3), and adding token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 in Table 4. The figures communicate the pipeline clearly, and the manuscript cites its principal model, dataset, and methodological foundations.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not establish the advantage of the proposed combination over closely related alternatives. Table 3 primarily compares against first-40-token selection and spatial grids; matched-budget class-attention top-k selection and existing token-merging methods such as the cited ToMe are missing. Consequently, the specific value of IQR-based adaptivity over established pruning and merging components remains uncertain.

Practical efficiency is insufficiently validated. Section 4.2 and Table 2 provide theoretical roofline estimates for LLM prefill, without measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or peak memory. Vision encoding, selection and merging overhead, autoregressive decoding, and batching variable token counts could materially affect deployment benefits.

The repeated claims of comparable performance understate meaningful losses. Even after fine-tuning, VQAv2 falls from 78.5 to 72.0 for 7B and from 80.0 to 72.8 for 13B; 13B MMBench falls from 67.7 to 62.3. Training-free POPE drops from 85.9 to 76.2 in Table 5. These losses may represent a useful compression tradeoff, but results at essentially one compression level do not characterize the available accuracy-efficiency operating range.

Important implementation details are missing or inconsistent. Algorithm 1 excludes the selected center from its neighbor search and replaces it with an unnormalized weighted sum of neighbors, whereas the prose describes preserving selected tokens and weighted averaging. The neighborhood size k, attention-head aggregation, and handling of overlapping clusters are unspecified. LoRA hyperparameters are also absent, and a promised code release does not resolve these reproducibility gaps in the supplied manuscript.

Experimental controls and evidence for adaptivity need strengthening. The main proposed models receive an additional epoch of LoRA training, without an equally fine-tuned full-token control to isolate the source of improvements. The claim that retained token counts track image complexity relies on a few visualizations, without quantitative token-count distributions or comparison against a fixed budget using the same importance scores. Validation is confined to one model family at 336-pixel resolution, leaving the high-resolution and video motivation untested.
